source: ../../src/read/old/dns.md (the old page 'DNS: resolution, caching, and the failure modes', saved verbatim by the root on 2026-10-05)
checked: 2026-10-05; primary sources in inputs/facts_checked.md and inline links; R<n> = Reading section n, R0 = one screen, T-pod / T-cache = tabs, M = Further reading

facts.old: Stub (libc getaddrinfo, asks one question, caches nothing), recursive (does the legwork, holds the cache), authoritative (never recurses)
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 1034 s5.3.3; glibc/musl recorded with no cache)

facts.old: Client-to-resolver leg recursive, resolver-to-root-to-TLD-to-authoritative iterative with referrals
facts.verdict: verified and recorded (lab walk from CoreDNS logs)

facts.old: 13 root server identities
facts.verdict: verified (root-servers.org, RSSAC023)

facts.old: roughly 1,900 anycast instances
facts.verdict: corrected: 2,045 operational instances on 2026-10-05 (root-servers.org)

facts.old: 13 is a legacy artifact of fitting the priming response into 512 bytes
facts.verdict: verified (RSSAC023 s2.6)

facts.old: QNAME minimisation RFC 9156, default in major resolvers; root no longer learns full query
facts.verdict: verified and recorded (Unbound default since 1.7.2; BIND relaxed default); root's log shows 'A test.' with it and 'A api.llm.test.' without

facts.old: UDP and TCP port 53, 12-byte header, labels 63, names 255, UDP 512
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 1035 s2.3.4, s4.1.1); real bytes parsed

facts.old: EDNS(0) RFC 6891: OPT record, larger payload size, DO bit, options (client subnet, cookies, padding)
facts.verdict: verified; OPT record shown in the recorded bytes

facts.old: DNS Flag Day 2020: 1232 bytes; 4096 default now harmful; fragmentation lossy and a poisoning vector
facts.verdict: verified (dnsflagday.net/2020)

facts.old: TC=1 then TCP retry; RFC 7766 makes TCP support mandatory; firewalls still block it
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 7766 s5) and recorded (pool.llm.test: 671 bytes over TCP, 682 with EDNS; glibc and musl both fell back to TCP)

facts.old: Compression 14-bit offset pointer reaches only the first 16,383 bytes
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 1035 s4.1.4); c0 0c pointer shown in recorded bytes

facts.old: Zone owner sets TTL per RRset; resolver counts down; no push, no invalidation
facts.verdict: verified and recorded (TTL change run)

facts.old: RFC 8767 serve-stale on by default in Unbound and BIND
facts.verdict: corrected: off by default in both (Unbound serve-expired: no; BIND 9.20 stale-answer-enable no); recorded with serve-expired yes: stale answer with TTL 30 after about 1.8 s

facts.old: Negative TTL = min(SOA MINIMUM, SOA TTL); RFC 2308 repurposed MINIMUM
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 2308 s5) and recorded (30 s in the lab; anthropic.com 1,800)

facts.old: MINIMUM 86400 caches a deleted record's NXDOMAIN for a day; fixing the record does not fix clients
facts.verdict: verified by arithmetic and the recorded run

facts.old: Negative caching covers NODATA as well as NXDOMAIN (bites AAAA queries for A-only services)
facts.verdict: NODATA covered: verified (RFC 2308 s2.2; recorded api.llm.test TXT). The AAAA-specific harm is not demonstrated and not repeated

facts.old: Keep SOA MINIMUM at 300 to 900 s on zones under active change
facts.verdict: kept as operating advice

facts.old: A/AAAA: getaddrinfo queries both in parallel (load-bearing for the conntrack race)
facts.verdict: recorded (both libraries send A and AAAA together from one socket)

facts.old: CNAME: no other data at a node with a CNAME (RFC 1034); illegal at apex
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 1034 s3.6.2, RFC 2181 s10.1)

facts.old: MX target must be A/AAAA name, never CNAME; null MX 0 . (RFC 7505)
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 2181 s10.3, RFC 7505); null MX in the lab zone

facts.old: TXT strings at most 255 octets, concatenated; SPF, DKIM, DMARC, verification; 2048-bit DKIM must be split
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 1035 s3.3) and shown with a real 2048-bit key split into two strings

facts.old: SRV _service._proto.name; Kubernetes publishes per service port
facts.verdict: verified (Kubernetes DNS docs); recorded SRV

facts.old: SOA fields
facts.verdict: verified; recorded

facts.old: CAA RFC 8659, mandatory for CAs since 2017
facts.verdict: verified (CA/B ballot 187, effective 2017-09-08)

facts.old: PTR under in-addr.arpa and ip6.arpa; rarely load-bearing
facts.verdict: kept

facts.old: SVCB/HTTPS RFC 9460: ALPN, port, IP hints, ech, apex aliasing
facts.verdict: verified (ech is reserved in RFC 9460 and defined elsewhere); real HTTPS records of api.anthropic.com (h2) and cloudflare.com (h3,h2) recorded

facts.old: Apex fixes: flattening (ANAME draft expired), Route 53 alias, HTTPS AliasMode
facts.verdict: verified (ANAME draft expired 2019; Route 53 alias free and allowed at apex; RFC 9460)

facts.old: Route 53 alias records take their TTL from the target and answer only when name and type match
facts.verdict: unconfirmed today; not repeated

facts.old: HTTPS AliasMode now supported by all major browsers
facts.verdict: unconfirmed today; not repeated

facts.old: Propagation is a myth; lower TTL one old-TTL period before; NS changes slow because .com delegations carry 48 h TTL
facts.verdict: verified (root zone file: com. 172800; .com delegations 172800 observed); simulated in the Cache timeline tab

facts.old: JVM caches forever under a SecurityManager, about 30 s otherwise
facts.verdict: corrected: true up to JDK 23; current JDK simply 30 s; negative cache 10 s (java.security)

facts.old: Python caches nothing; requests/urllib3 add no cache; fresh Session per request resolves every call
facts.verdict: verified (Python docs) and recorded: 80 queries for 10 requests with new connections, 8 with one kept-alive connection, 80 when the server closes connections

facts.old: A training loop pulling from S3 generates five-figure QPS at CoreDNS
facts.verdict: unconfirmed figure; mechanism kept without the number

facts.old: glibc sequential nameservers, 5 s timeout, single-request, single-request-reopen, use-vc; musl parallel, none of those options
facts.verdict: verified (resolv.conf(5), musl wiki) and recorded (dead first server: glibc 5.0 s, musl under 10 ms; lost packet: glibc 5.0 s, musl 2.5 s)

facts.old: Lowering ndots can break Alpine pods where it works on Debian
facts.verdict: verified and recorded: kubernetes.default with ndots:1 resolves on glibc, fails on musl

facts.old: Prefer glibc base images for ML containers
facts.verdict: kept as advice, supported by the recordings

facts.old: ndots:5: s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com gives five sequential queries, four NXDOMAIN, ten packets
facts.verdict: corrected: depends on the search list. With the three Kubernetes domains a two- or three-dot name is 4 names x 2 types = 8 queries, 6 NXDOMAIN (recorded); ten queries with a fourth, node-inherited domain (recorded)

facts.old: Fixes: trailing dot, dnsConfig ndots 1, NodeLocal DNSCache, CoreDNS autopath
facts.verdict: verified (Kubernetes docs, CoreDNS autopath); trailing dot recorded (2 queries)

facts.old: Lowering ndots breaks bare short names like myservice
facts.verdict: corrected: recorded, a name with no dot still resolves (0 dots is below ndots); names with a dot break, on musl only

facts.old: Conntrack: three races; first two fixed in Linux 4.17; third never fixed in-kernel
facts.verdict: corrected: fixes in 4.19, 5.0 and (third, for UDP) 5.6 (kernel commits); Weave blog archived

facts.old: Symptom: clean 5-second spike (glibc default timeout)
facts.verdict: recorded: 5,037 ms for one lost packet

facts.old: NodeLocal DNSCache on 169.254.20.10, bypasses DNAT, upgrades upstream to TCP, stable since 1.18
facts.verdict: verified (docs; 169.254.20.10 is the add-on README's default)

facts.old: CoreDNS forward to /etc/resolv.conf with systemd-resolved 127.0.0.53 loops; loop plugin crashes the pod; leading cause of CrashLoopBackOff on new clusters
facts.verdict: verified (CoreDNS loop docs, Kubernetes DNS debugging) and recorded (loop plugin FATAL, exit 1); 'leading cause' not verified, not repeated

facts.old: CoreDNS CPU-bound, no HPA by default; alarm on NXDOMAIN rate
facts.verdict: kept in substance ('replica count does not follow cluster size unless you add an autoscaler'); NXDOMAIN share recorded (6 of 8)

facts.old: VPC resolver limited to 1,024 packets per second per ENI; drops surface as timeouts
facts.verdict: corrected: the documented quota is 1,024 packets per second for link-local services in aggregate (DNS, IMDS, time sync), not increasable

facts.old: Private hosted zones split horizon; enableDnsSupport/enableDnsHostnames; Resolver endpoints both directions, billed per query
facts.verdict: verified in substance (AWS VPC DNS docs); billing detail not re-fetched, stated generally

facts.old: Route 53 health checks 30 s / 10 s, threshold 3, require public endpoint; CloudWatch alarm for private
facts.verdict: verified (HealthCheckConfig, health-check types)

facts.old: Routing policies weighted, latency, failover, multivalue (up to 8)
facts.verdict: verified

facts.old: Headless service returns one A per ready endpoint; StatefulSet stable ordinal names
facts.verdict: verified (Kubernetes docs) and recorded (myjob-headless: four addresses)

facts.old: publishNotReadyAddresses: true; deadlock is the single most common cause of torchrun hanging at initialisation
facts.verdict: field and use verified (Service API); 'single most common cause' unconfirmed, softened to 'worth checking'

facts.old: Ray needs DNS only to find the head node (GCS on 6379)
facts.verdict: unconfirmed today; not repeated

facts.old: Multi-replica vLLM behind a real router, not DNS round-robin
facts.verdict: kept as advice in general form

facts.old: DNSSEC: origin, integrity, authenticated denial; chain from root anchor via DS and DNSKEY; no confidentiality, no stub hop, worse amplification
facts.verdict: verified (RFC 4033-4035) and recorded on a signed lab tree (valid, expired, rolled, NSEC proof)

facts.old: About 36% of users behind validating resolvers, about 7% of zones signed, flat for twenty years
facts.verdict: corrected: 39.65% full + 9.41% partial (APNIC, 2026-10-03); 5.0% of .com with DS (Verisign, 2026-10-03/05); 'flat for twenty years' not repeated

facts.old: .de 2026-05-05: non-validatable signatures during KSK rollover; SERVFAIL; Cloudflare marked .de insecure hours later
facts.verdict: verified with detail (DENIC: key tag 33834, three key pairs one published, about three hours; Cloudflare NTA-like override 22:17 UTC)

facts.old: DoT RFC 7858 853/TCP blockable; DoH RFC 8484 on 443; DoQ RFC 9250 853/UDP
facts.verdict: verified; DoT used for every public lookup on this page

facts.old: 2026 measurements: DoQ median 88 ms vs 883 ms, at most 1% page-load difference
facts.verdict: unconfirmed (not found); replaced by Kosek et al. IMC 2022

facts.old: Kaminsky 2008, 16-bit ID; RFC 5452 port randomisation; cookies; 0x20; SAD DNS 2020 ICMP side channel fixed by randomising
facts.verdict: verified (CERT VU#800113, RFC 5452, RFC 7873, draft-vixie, saddns.net, kernel commit)

facts.old: Rebinding: TTL 0, same-origin keyed on name; Jupyter, Ray, MLflow, TensorBoard, vLLM on 0.0.0.0 reachable
facts.verdict: verified (HTML same-origin) and recorded against an agent fetch tool; Chrome Local Network Access added

facts.old: SSRF time-of-check bypass; resolve once, validate IP, connect to literal IP with Host header; IMDSv2 hop limit 1
facts.verdict: verified and recorded (naive leaked, pinned did not); hop-limit nuance from AWS docs

facts.old: Exfiltration through labels; SUNBURST used exactly this; detection by cardinality, entropy, NXDOMAIN ratio; Route 53 Resolver query logging off by default
facts.verdict: verified with nuance (SUNBURST: DNS first stage, HTTP for main C2); query logging opt-in

facts.old: dig tool commands (+short, @ns +norecurse, +trace, SOA, +dnssec, +cd, -x, +nsid); TTL countdown reading; delv, kdig, doggo; nslookup discouraged
facts.verdict: kept; nslookup history verified (BIND CHANGES 1700); +trace limitation behind interception added

facts.old: Compare three answers: authoritative, your resolver, public
facts.verdict: kept

facts.old: AWS us-east-1 2025-10-19: three Enactors race, empty record, manual repair, DynamoDB impact 14 h 32 m
facts.verdict: mechanism verified; duration corrected: DNS impact 11:48 PM to about 2:25 AM PDT, clients recovered by 2:40 AM; 14 h 32 m is the whole event

facts.old: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 2025-07-14: config error from 6 June dormant five weeks; 62 minutes; BGP hijack misreported
facts.verdict: verified (Cloudflare post-mortem)

facts.old: Root KSK rollover 2026-10-11, KSK-2024 key tag 38696; RFC 5011 not guaranteed; stale anchors in images top risk
facts.verdict: verified (IANA, ICANN); real root key set recorded; key tags recomputed and matched to IANA; stale-anchor failure reproduced in the lab

facts.old: Connections: UDP payload limits (networking foundations), CAA and 10-day validation reuse (TLS), HTTPS record and ECH (TLS), service discovery (ml-infra)
facts.verdict: links kept; the certificate validation-reuse detail is owned by the TLS page

facts.old: Best resources: RFC 1034/1035, RFC 9499, RFC 2308, Kubernetes DNS spec, ndots:5 explained, racy conntrack, AWS summary, ICANN KSK
facts.verdict: all kept, link-checked; racy conntrack points at the archived Weave post
